key: In the same way the sage is always skilful at saving men, and so he does not cast away any man; he is always skilful at saving things, and so he does not cast away anything.
s: The chapter says the sage, always skilful at saving men and things, casts none away; Wang Bi, on chapter 27, reads it as the sage setting up no forms and names to check things and no path of advancement that sets apart and casts off the unworthy, but aiding all things to be so of themselves.
src: Wang Bi, Laozi zhu, chapter 27, zh.wikisource (the Huating Zhang edition), revision 2354026 (2024)

evidence.words: 聖人不立形名以檢於物，不造進向以殊棄不肖，輔萬物之自然而不為始，故曰無棄人也。
evidence.gloss: The sage does not set up forms and names by which to check things, and does not create paths of advancement by which to set apart and cast off the unworthy; he aids all things in being so of themselves and does not make himself their beginning. Therefore the text says he casts away no man.
